author: artificialanlys
text:
Announcing Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1: a shift toward agentic workloads, featuring upgraded benchmarks and new per-task metrics

The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is our synthesis metric for assessing model intelligence and tracking AI progress. v4.1 marks a broader shift toward agentic workloads, with three main changes:

Updated and reweighted evaluations toward agentic tasks:
1. We upgraded three evaluations, removed one, and reweighted the Intelligence Index: 
➤ Upgraded Terminal-Bench Hard to Terminal-Bench 2.1 and τ²-Bench Telecom to τ³-Bench Banking. Both move to newer, more robust task sets with harder, more realistic agentic scenarios that better separate frontier models 
➤ Upgraded GDPval-AA to GDPval-AA v2. The upgrade re-baselines Elo to human performance at 1000, introduces a rotating panel of frontier-model judges, and raises the turn limit from 100 to 250 for longer-horizon agent trajectories 
➤ Removed IFBench due to saturation. The benchmark no longer distinguishes frontier models sufficiently, so we have removed it from the Intelligence Index. We will continue to run it and publish results on new model releases

2. Cost per Task, Time per Task, and Tokens per Task:
Three new per-task metrics, reported for every model and based on the Intelligence Index. We take the total cost, total time, and total output tokens for a model to run the Intelligence Index and divide by the number of tasks across its evaluations, giving the average cost, time, and output tokens to complete a single Intelligence Index task

3. Cached input token reporting:
We now report cached input tokens and their impact on cost, including the cost to run the Intelligence Index, to better reflect the real cost of running each model

Key Results:
➤ Leading models: Claude Fable 5 (with Opus 4.8 fallback, 60) leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1 by four points but is currently unavailable, leaving Claude Opus 4.8 (max, 56) as the most intelligent available model, ahead of GPT-5.5 (xhigh, 55) ➤ Open weights leading models: Among open weights models, DeepSeek V4 Pro (max, 44) and MiniMax M3 (44) lead, followed by Kimi K2.6 (43) and MiMo-V2.5-Pro (42) 
➤Cost per Task: Claude Opus 4.8 (max) is the most expensive available model at $1.78 per task, with Claude Fable 5 the highest overall at $3.25. GPT-5.5 (xhigh) scores within a point of Opus 4.8 on the Intelligence Index at $0.99 per task. DeepSeek V4 Pro (max) stands out on the Intelligence vs Cost per Task chart at $0.04 per task, with other leading proprietary models costing 20x to 45x more 
➤Time per Task: time per task (inference decode time) ranges from 1.5 minutes for Grok 4.3 (high) to 13.5 for Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max), a roughly 9x spread. Claude Opus 4.8 (max) completes a task in 6.4 minutes and GPT-5.5 (xhigh) in 3.7, while Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview stands out on the Intelligence vs Time per Task chart at 1.6 minutes for a score of 46

author: cyrilxbt
text:
SOMEONE LEAKED THE FULL SYSTEM PROMPT OF CLAUDE FABLE 5 — AND IT'S SITTING ON GITHUB WITH 26,000 STARS.

Anthropic launched Fable 5 on June 9.
The prompt was public within 24 hours.

120,000 characters.
1,585 lines.
27,000 tokens.
Every hidden instruction exposed.

CL4R1T4S repo by Pliny the Liberator.
The same repo that previously leaked ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Cursor, Lovable, Replit, and Perplexity.

Here is what it actually reveals:

Fable 5 and Mythos 5 share the same underlying model. Fable gets extra safety layers. Mythos doesn't, but is restricted to approved organizations only.

Knowledge cutoff is end of January 2026. Not May. Not March. January.

Claude is explicitly instructed to avoid bullet points, headers, and lists unless the user asks. That question everyone had about why Claude writes in prose now is answered in line 847.

Copyright hard limit: quoting 15 or more words from any single source is flagged as a severe violation. One quote per source maximum. After one quote, that source is closed.

A new persistent storage API lets artifacts store and retrieve data across sessions using key-value pairs.

MCP app connectors are built directly into the prompt. Claude can search for and suggest third-party integrations mid-conversation.

The prompt includes detailed instructions for Claude Cowork, Claude in Chrome, Claude in Excel, and Claude in PowerPoint.

This prompt is specific to https://t.co/pkYQR1hV09's consumer interface. API users get no system prompt. Claude Code has its own separate instructions entirely.

700,000 views in the first two days.
26,400 GitHub stars.
4,700 forks.

author: rickyho_1989
text:
The charts highlight something that many investors still underestimate: AI is rapidly becoming a scale business rather than a pure technology business.

At the frontier, Anthropic remains the intelligence leader. Claude Fable 5 scores 60 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ahead of Opus 4.8 at 56 and GPT-5.5 at 55. However, the second chart shows that this final increment of intelligence comes at a very steep cost. Fable 5 costs roughly $3.25 per benchmark task versus $1.78 for Opus 4.8 and $0.99 for GPT-5.5.

In other words, Anthropic appears to be operating on the far right side of the efficiency curve where each additional point of intelligence requires disproportionately more compute, more reasoning tokens, and more inference cost. The company currently owns the performance crown, but it is paying heavily for it.

The more interesting story is happening below the frontier. DeepSeek V4 Pro Max delivers 44 intelligence points for around $0.06 per task. MiMo V2.5 Pro delivers 42 points for roughly the same cost. Gemini Flash reaches 50 points while remaining dramatically cheaper than the frontier models. The intelligence gap between the best and the “good enough” models remains meaningful, but the cost gap is becoming enormous.

This is exactly what happens when a technology industry starts to mature. The market initially competes on absolute performance. Eventually it begins competing on performance per dollar.

The scatter plot makes this particularly clear. The most attractive area is not necessarily the top-right corner where intelligence is highest. It is the upper-left area where intelligence remains high while costs collapse. Many Chinese models now sit squarely in that region.

This is why the narrative that “the cheapest model wins” is just as wrong as the narrative that “the smartest model wins.” Neither is sufficient. The winners are likely to be the models that sit on the Pareto frontier, delivering the highest intelligence for a given cost level. Today that frontier includes Anthropic at the very high end, Google in the middle, and a growing group of Chinese labs including DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax, and Xiaomi at the efficiency end.

For investors, this has an important implication. Falling inference costs are not necessarily bearish for AI infrastructure. Historically, lower computing costs have almost always led to more consumption rather than less. We saw it with storage, bandwidth, cloud computing, and semiconductors. As intelligence becomes cheaper, companies simply run more agents, automate more workflows, and expand AI usage into new domains.

The charts therefore reinforce a view that we have held for some time: AI is not becoming less valuable because models are getting cheaper. AI is becoming more ubiquitous because models are getting cheaper.

Anthropic currently leads the intelligence race. Chinese labs are increasingly leading the efficiency race. Google appears to be competing effectively across both dimensions. The result is an industry that is simultaneously moving up the intelligence curve and down the cost curve. That combination is exactly what drives mass adoption.

The most bullish takeaway is that the industry is no longer trading off intelligence against cost. It is increasingly improving both at the same time. Historically, that is the hallmark of a technology entering its exponential adoption phase rather than approaching saturation.

author: altmasterroshi
text:
$DOT @usedotai is beginning to outperform other AI privacy projects out there, and it’s pretty clear to me that it’ll soon be a leader

How It Outperforms Other Projects

The key advantage is compound/ensemble intelligence rather than raw single-model power. Here’s the direct comparison from their transparent 30-task benchmark (hard synthetic builder tasks across privacy infra, routing, API design, agent safety, debugging, evals, model-layer decentralization, etc.; 5 routes tested, 150 real streamed completions, rubric-scored):

Benchmark Results (Mean Rubric Score out of ~100):

•  Dot Supercharged: 86.2 (Pass rate 90%, Excellent 22/30 tasks)
•  Dot Qwen 3.6 Plus (open baseline): 79.0
•  Claude Opus 4.8 (frontier baseline): 77.4
•  OpenAI GPT-5.5 (frontier baseline): 74.5
•  Dot Gemma 4 (fast baseline): 67.3
Other wins for Supercharged:
•  Best score floor (worst-task performance)
•  Highest excellent rate
•  Strongest overall on “best score + floor”
•  +7.2 points vs. best single route

Why this beats single-model projects (Claude, GPT, Gemini, etc.):

•  Single models answer independently. Dot Supercharged runs multiple, cross-checks, critiques, and synthesizes — leading to higher final-answer quality, fewer errors, and better handling of nuance/edge cases on hard builder tasks.

•  It improves the “score floor” (consistency on tough tasks) where single models often drop.

Uncensored / refusal resistance (big differentiator vs. heavily safety-aligned models like Fable-5):

•  Fable-5 (and similar over-aligned models) frequently refuses or degrades on basic factual/scientific questions (biology, medicine, etc.).

•  Dot Supercharged answered 10/10 test prompts (cell membranes, mitochondria, prions, mRNA vaccines, Ebola, antibiotic resistance, etc.) with 0 refusals, 0 errors, and no degraded fallbacks. It uses a routed panel + synthesis layer instead of a single fragile safety gate.

This update doesn’t just add another model — it introduces a superior compound inference system that demonstrably outperforms standalone frontier models and many alternative approaches on Dot’s target use cases (hard technical/building tasks) while doubling down on privacy, anonymity, and reduced over-refusal. It directly supports their claim of “objectively better AI.”

All eyes on what @stagedhappen is building here

How one guy is printing $5,300/month running an AI girl account

The craziest part? He completely automated the system and only works 40 minutes a day.

Here’s how he built the entire system from scratch.

The Tech Stack:

- Claude Fable 5
- ComfyUI + Flux
- Kling 3.0
- Fanvue MCP

Step-by-step instructions:

1. Finding the Meta

He didn't guess, he asked Claude to analyze the market and find an untapped, high-growth niche. 

The winning prompt? A 20-year-old Alt/Emo e-girl.

Using pre-built Flux workflows in ComfyUI, he mass-generated a consistent face-swapped profile picture, 

a clean Instagram grid, and a bank of semi-NSFW content for the paid audience.

3. Hacking Viral Traffic

Static images don't work at all. 

He used Kling 3.0 to generate 9:16 video clips of the AI model moving, then asked Claude for 30 viral text hooks,

Result: One reel hit 600k+ views in month two.

He linked his Fanvue to Claude so the AI actually reads fan chats, figures out what to charge, and replies just like the model would.

With that infrastructure he hit 800+ IG followers, 50 paid subscribers, and crossed the $5.3k mark with minimal ad spend. 

You don't need a team or a massive budget anymore. Just set up the stack and let it run.

author: bonduelleioat
text:
Are you buying a business-class ticket for your backpack? 

That’s exactly what you’re doing with your AI budget when the most expensive intelligence, Fable 5, is performing the work of a dirt-cheap linter. 

The biggest expense in most AI bills isn’t task complexity - it’s developer anxiety. Trying to play it safe, teams throw absolutely every routine task at a $50 flagship model, from renaming variables to writing docstrings.

As a result, 80% of the budget is spent on tasks that free or low-cost models handle just as well.

Optimization begins when you stop thinking in terms of “models” and start thinking in terms of roles.

One expensive brain (Fable 5) is only needed as the architect and coordinator of the process.

The bulk of coding should be handled by Sonnet by default. 

Complex isolated bugs can be escalated to Opus, while pass/fail verification is performed by Haiku, which costs ten times less than the flagship model.

The model that writes the code should never be the one reviewing it - that’s the job of a cheap, independent controller.

This division of responsibilities, combined with context freezing for prompt caching and running overnight jobs through the Batch API at a 50% discount, can instantly cut the final bill by 71%.

AI only becomes a profitable business tool when you stop paying professor-level rates for intern-level work.

🔥 Học sinh trung học nhưng có 2 ông thầy cơ bự - Model coding 12B đang được cộng đồng Local AI bàn tán nhiều nhất tuần này trên Hugging Face kết hợp cả fable5 và composer 2.5

Một trong những model đang nổi lên trên Hugging Face là gemma-4-12B-coder-fable5-composer2.5-v1, phiên bản fine-tune từ Gemma 4 12B được tối ưu riêng cho lập trình và suy luận mã nguồn. Chỉ sau thời gian ngắn phát hành, model đã nhanh chóng xuất hiện trong nhiều cuộc thảo luận của cộng đồng Local LLM và Vibe Coding. (Hugging Face⁠￼)

Các điểm nổi bật:

* Xây dựng trên nền tảng Gemma 4 12B mới nhất của Google.
* Tối ưu riêng cho Python và các bài toán lập trình.
* Huấn luyện từ các bộ dữ liệu có kiểm chứng bằng unit test.
* Kết hợp dữ liệu Composer 2.5 và Fable 5 để cải thiện khả năng reasoning.
* Hỗ trợ chế độ “thinking” trước khi sinh mã nguồn.
* Chạy hoàn toàn local, không cần API.
* Hỗ trợ GGUF cho llama.cpp, LM Studio, Jan và Open WebUI.
* Có các phiên bản từ Q2 đến Q8 phù hợp nhiều cấu hình phần cứng.
* Bản Q2 chỉ khoảng 4.5GB VRAM/RAM hợp nhất. (Hugging Face⁠￼)

Điều khiến model này được chú ý không phải vì kích thước 12B, mà vì triết lý huấn luyện khá thú vị: chỉ giữ lại các chain-of-thought dẫn tới lời giải vượt qua kiểm thử tự động. Điều này giúp mô hình học từ các quá trình suy luận thực sự tạo ra mã nguồn chạy đúng thay vì chỉ học từ câu trả lời cuối cùng. (Hugging Face⁠￼)

Phù hợp cho:

* Claude Code thay thế chạy local.
* Agent lập trình trên Open WebUI.
* VS Code + Continue/Cline.
* Tự động sinh script Python.
* Học thuật toán và competitive programming.
* Homelab AI không muốn phụ thuộc cloud.

Một trong những model đang nổi lên trên Hugging Face là gemma-4-12B-coder-fable5-composer2.5-v1, phiên bản fine-tune từ Gemma 4 12B được tối ưu riêng cho lập trình và suy luận mã nguồn. Chỉ sau thời gian ngắn phát hành, model đã nhanh chóng xuất hiện trong nhiều cuộc thảo luận của cộng đồng Local LLM và Vibe Coding. (Hugging Face⁠￼)

Các điểm nổi bật:

* Xây dựng trên nền tảng Gemma 4 12B mới nhất của Google.
* Tối ưu riêng cho Python và các bài toán lập trình.
* Huấn luyện từ các bộ dữ liệu có kiểm chứng bằng unit test.
* Kết hợp dữ liệu Composer 2.5 và Fable 5 để cải thiện khả năng reasoning.
* Hỗ trợ chế độ “thinking” trước khi sinh mã nguồn.
* Chạy hoàn toàn local, không cần API.
* Hỗ trợ GGUF cho llama.cpp, LM Studio, Jan và Open WebUI.
* Có các phiên bản từ Q2 đến Q8 phù hợp nhiều cấu hình phần cứng.
* Bản Q2 chỉ khoảng 4.5GB VRAM/RAM hợp nhất. (Hugging Face⁠￼)

Điều khiến model này được chú ý không phải vì kích thước 12B, mà vì triết lý huấn luyện khá thú vị: chỉ giữ lại các chain-of-thought dẫn tới lời giải vượt qua kiểm thử tự động. Điều này giúp mô hình học từ các quá trình suy luận thực sự tạo ra mã nguồn chạy đúng thay vì chỉ học từ câu trả lời cuối cùng. (Hugging Face⁠￼)

Phù hợp cho:

* Claude Code thay thế chạy local.
* Agent lập trình trên Open WebUI.
* VS Code + Continue/Cline.
* Tự động sinh script Python.
* Học thuật toán và competitive programming.
* Homelab AI không muốn phụ thuộc cloud.

Nếu bạn đang sở hữu GPU 8GB–16GB hoặc MacBook Apple Silicon và muốn có một coding model mạnh nhưng vẫn chạy được hoàn toàn offline, đây là một trong những model đáng thử nhất của hệ sinh thái Gemma 4 hiện tại. (Hugging Face⁠￼)

author: anton_bursa
text:
Jake Fitzgerald asked Claude Fable 5 to design a QDD actuator. 30 minutes, 400k tokens, working CAD model with animated gearbox and collision validation.

What he got from one prompt: a 4.5:1 planetary reduction stage, properly meshed gear train, exploded view animation tied to a parametric slider. The visualizer interface itself was generated by Fable in the same run.

This is the part the CAD industry hasn't priced in yet. SolidWorks and Fusion 360 sell $4,000/year licenses to people who needed an expert tool. Most of those people just wanted to describe what they need and get a working part.

The shift coming: engineering firms that build AI-first design workflow as a moat.

Save this. The conversation is about to start.

author: paulsolt
text:
One of the challenges of working with AI is that it sometimes FAILS to do what you want.

This weekend it felt like whack-a-mole with BUGS.

One bug would be fixed by the agent, only to break something unrelated.

THREE things helped:
1. More focused tests and the logging
2. Dedicated research tasks on the APIs agents struggled with (Using my Librarian skill)
3. Slowing down and requesting less fixes all at once

#1 Normally when I'm driving agents, they fix things fast, but around areas that are hard like window managment, AppKit/SwiftUI integration, and focus, agents tend to struggle.

Agents are willing to waste a lot of time running your full test suite, when they really only need to test the new functionality first, before regression testing. You waste a lot of time waiting for agents who run too many slow tests when your still in active development.

On the other side, logs with the Telemetry skill has helped agents review run-time behaviors to triage complex app lifecycle issues. This OpenAI skill is in Build macOS/iOS Apps Plugin (Thanks @Dimillian !)

#2 Sometimes agents will say something is possible ... which I know isn't true, but they still fail to get the result I want.

I have a Librarian skill that requires code samples with proof (screenshots or video). This forces agents to try multiple approaches to find a solution.

The "production" agents were stuck in SwiftUI-land when they should have been working in AppKit ... I guess I could have given more guidance on where to look, but I assumed they could see the whole picture. 

#3 To really help, I had to take a step back, make fewer requests, so that the critical problems could be solved first. It took way longer than I expected, but it feels really good right now.

I asked agents to use "Fresh eyes" and to "take a step back" to consider other solutions.

Both Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 felt like they were underperforming, probably because I was trying to drive them too fast without enough fast verification loops.

Fable 5 really felt next level, and I'm hoping we get more agents of that caliber soon.

Here's the new onboarding for Super Easy Timer.

I had a lot of Fable tokens to use up before my weekly reset, so I made this live 3D map of London with Three.js

Every train, bus, boat and plane is real and live right now!

- Tube, bus and riverboat data from TfL
- National Rail trains from Darwin live departure boards
- ADS-B for planes and helicopters
- AIS feed for boats and ships
- Map data from Overture and OpenStreetMap

Trains and buses have no GPS feed, so their positions are inferred from arrival countdowns and departure boards, then animated along the track/route geometry

author: ecrivaine_k
text:
關於 AI 和教育。

今天看到 @mattshumer_ 加入 Alpha School，簡單研究了一下他們的教育模式，發現很適合快速擴張。

這是一家用 AI 重構 K-12 教育的美國私立學校網絡。目前在美國有 25 個校區，有暑期項目可以申請，收費大概 7,500~ 12500 萬美元 / 五周。

核心模式： 

學生每天只用 約 2 小時，透過個人化 AI tutor 完成所有核心學科（數學、英文、科學等），強調 mastery-based（完全掌握才繼續）。 下午用來做 workshops、生活技能、熱情項目、運動、創業體驗等「真實世界能力」培養。

簡單説：上午密集學習靠 AI 做定制化，狂學，依然保留人類教師引導和班級社交互動，下午做人類依然該做的事，積纍數據給家長回家繼續用。

這種模式，和中國科幻作家郝景芳老師開的童行書院，在課程設置上其實有不少相似之處。

但在 AI 輔助下，即使在美國，這種「AI + 真實項目」的模式，成本也比傳統全人類教師的模式低不少。

我看了一下他們公開的課程案例，發現其中不少內容，其實在家裡或小圈子裡就能實現一部分。

舉幾個例子：

1⃣ K-1（幼兒園～一年級）有「AI Storybook Authors」課程：

孩子用 AI 寫故事、生成插圖，最後真正出版一本精裝書，還要上台朗讀給家長聽，主要讓小孩去掌握適合他們自己的 prompt engineering。

這是我覺得最容易在家實現的一個。 

家長不需要精通 prompt engineering，基本做好篩選和激勵就有很大幫助。而中國印刷一本精裝繪本成本極低，還有大量面向兒童創作者的發布渠道，可以讓孩子獲得真實反饋。

btw 想起我小時候，每周都手繪周刊，賣給我爸媽，獲得零花錢，但最終觸發了奇怪的技能點，周刊變日報，還送贈品（自製玩具），多買多優惠，最終還賣給了家族的其他小朋友，把他們零花錢都賺走了（不好意思跑題了~~

2⃣ 2-3 年級 有「AI Toy Inventors」：

學習基礎 3D 建模並列印出實體原型，與 AI 共同做頭腦風暴、做出產品、撰寫 sales pitch，家長和當地投資人共同參與學生推銷活動；還有無人機相關的課程，學生之間要做競賽。

→ 早在兩年前，也有工程師 DAO 友一直用 AI 輔助，給剛上小學的兒子做游戲編程學習課，效果很不錯。如果是圈内朋友，這一點也完全可以組團實現。

→ 之前其他 nomad 朋友提到，如果大部分人開始有小孩，其實 @balajis  的 The Network School 就很適合有這種 for kids 的活動，因爲作爲父母的參與者本身也是來自不同背景的科技從業者，可以配合 AI 去做這種實驗和產出。

3⃣ 6-8 年級 有 AI + Engineering 的課程： 

中學生要親手打造會自己瞄準的投石機、智慧溫室系統，結合感測器數據和 AI vibe coding。

→ 家長用心的話，拿出兩天時間，用樹莓派 + Grok Build，把 X 上相關的硬件用法自動整理一下，因材施教帶孩子做一兩個完整項目，全程記錄迭代過程，再讓 AI 幫忙整理學習軌跡，定系統學習計劃。

→ 在中國，做硬件嘗試的成本遠遠低於其他國家，物流速度也有先天優勢；與中國跨境物流渠道成熟的日本和東南亞，也可以藉助這個優勢。

但我認為這件事最難的地方不在技術，而在家長的精力與判斷力。

家長很難同時做到：

1. 判斷 AI 生成的內容是否正確
2. 做好教學設計與引導
3. 還有餘力沉澱整個過程的數據和迭代

現階段，用大多數模型去實現這些目標，依然需要頻繁的人工介入，除了 Fable 5 可以不用 Superpower 框架，以出色的統籌能力去兜底這種多元内容的系統設計，相對減輕人力投入成本。

對很多有小孩、不缺錢、但缺充足時間的家長來說，可能還是更愿意直接花錢上這類暑期學校。

Alpha School 這類擴張速度極快的學校，本身就是大企業對接當地資源的方式，古往今來都是最好的生意之一。

但未來一定會有更多工具和產品出現，填補家長無法全職投入的空缺，比如，像類似 Fitbit 記錄運動那樣，記錄學習軌跡。

只不過，不同背景家庭的小孩，在這種「AI 放大器」面前，能力差距可能會比現在拉得更大。

之前有接觸過母嬰 + AI 領域的初創項目，現在也想多認識在 AI + 育兒方向深耕的朋友。如果你在做相關產品，無論早期探索還是融資階段，都歡迎交流~

author: keiiuemura
text:
日本で開発している自分は今、世界最強と言われたAIモデルを使えない。性能でも価格でもなく、持っているパスポートが日本のものだから。Anthropic の Fable 5 の話で、地政学ニュースとして消費されているけれど、個人開発者の足元に直接効くので書いておく。

時系列はこうだ。6/9、Anthropic は Mythos 系統で初めて一般公開した Fable 5 を出した。SWE-Bench Pro 80.3%、次点に大差。自分も6/12に「諦めていた案件リストを全部見直す」と書いたばかりだった。その同じ6/12の金曜夕方、米政府が国家安全保障を理由に export control を発令。Anthropic は Fable 5 と Mythos 5 を全世界で停止した。理由は「ジェイルブレイク手法が見つかった」疑い（Amazon のセキュリティチームがホワイトハウスに報告したと報じられている）。

効いてくるのは停止そのものより、停止の「線の引き方」だ。公式声明にこう書いてある——「米国内外を問わず、あらゆる外国籍の人物（外国籍の Anthropic 社員を含む）のアクセスを停止せよ」。中国だけ、という話ではない。日本のパスポートを持つ自分も、アメリカに住む外国籍のエンジニアも、Anthropic 社内の外国籍社員すら、一律で締め出された。AIが性能ではなく国籍で人を選別した、おそらく初めての事例だ。

自分が更新したのは、ワークフローの「単一モデル依存」をやめること。半年、Claude Code 中心に深く組んできて、フロンティア1本に寄りかかる設計になっていた。でも今回でわかった。最高性能のモデルは、自分の落ち度ゼロで一晩で消える。しかも次は値上げでも障害でもなく、政治判断で。だから今週やったのは、主力を失っても回るように、Opus 4.8 と非米国系モデルで同じタスクが流れるか試すことだった。具体的には、プロンプトを特定モデル前提で書かない、モデル指定を一箇所にまとめて差し替え可能にする、評価用のタスクセットを手元に置いて乗り換え時に性能を測れるようにする。「エンジンを載せ替えても車の作りは変えなくていい」状態を、平時のうちに作っておく。

誤解してほしくないのは、Fable 5 を悪く言いたいわけではないこと。ホワイトハウスの David Sacks も「安全性が直れば解除する」と言っていて、数週間で戻る可能性は十分ある。Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5 は今も普通に使える。でも仮に Fable 5 が戻ってきても、今回の教訓は消えない。AIのベンダー選びに「性能・価格・コンテキスト長」だけでなく「政治的に切られないか」という軸が、個人レベルでも本当に要るようになった。

明日いちばん使っているモデルへのアクセスを失っても、自分の手元は止まらない設計になっているか。一度だけ確かめておくといい。自分はなっていなかった。

https://t.co/XFjO0JxsFf

author: scorenterprises
text:
I've been seeing a lot of people talk about Fable 5/Mythos so here's my 2 cents.

I read someone say "... it felt like I was in 2023 again" and honestly that was the best way I've seen it described.

Personally what I am working on, I use API's that are well documented, but probably don't have a lot of open source code written around them. So sometimes the AI just really can't help me there.

But in other areas where I have a well thought out plan of attack, or am doing something routine and fundamental, Fable 5 was pretty sweet.

I don't think there's anything it can do that other models can't do, but I do think it had the best "discretion" and it was chill. It would do the thing and not mess with the other parts of my codebase.

Personally I hate when people give the LLM's human emotions. It's a stochastic next token predictor, it doesn't care about you and is nothing without you. YOU are what is special in this process.

But it did seem nice, it felt like it was more receptive and careful and considerate of the other code.

It's great if you're making something where you can be an expert on a topic, and prompt the syntax. You must review that code though. Software engineering is not solved. Make it adhere to conventions and patterns for maintainability.

The next gripe I have with it is cost. That mf BURNS through tokens, and they weren't shy to tell you 2x what Opus consumes. 

The costs are just stupid at this point though. I can't stand when I see people post their Anthropic bill. If you truly were able to think critically and understand the problems you should be able to do more with less. That is literally the pinnacle of being good at something is making it simple.

Simple does not mean easy.

But there's no way a team of engineers can ship meaningful features to meaningful projects in a cost effective way. 

There's just no way bro.

I see a future where engineers are allocated x amount of tokens and if you accomplish your tasks under x tokens you can either stack the token quota, get more, or take a bonus.

But then there's the political view of what the Fable 5 ban means.

Even with all of Anthropic's safe guards people were still able to jail break that model on release day. I'm not sure they'll ever be able to solve that issue. Fable 5 was very sensitive to user input and was still jail broken.

AI labs need to be careful how they market this stuff because now the government has shown they are not shy to ban models. 

Also hardware providers need to understand that there could be regulations on shipping their chips internationally. Yes Jenson we care more about national security and leading the AI race more than your bottom line. That interview annoyed me ifykyk.

The bottom line I have for this, is it's just a better tool. not a replacement.

The 80 20 rule is strengthened here. Most projects failed before 60 was reached. Now they get nuked quicker with more built out.

Eventually we'll all have local models and tokens will be really cheap... I hope.

author: trifon_getsov
text:
The most dangerous thing about the AI ban on Fable 5 isn't the ban.

It's that a government just demonstrated it can flip a switch and remove the most capable reasoning tool on earth from an entire category of people overnight, in 90mins.

No warning. 
No appeal.
 No timeline.

And the conversation immediately became about whether the model was actually dangerous, as if that's the relevant question.

It isn't.

The relevant question is: 

what does it mean to build your business, your research, your workflow, on infrastructure that can be politically revoked faster than your rent is due?

The developers who felt nothing when this happened are the ones with the most exposure. 

They've just built a dependency they haven't priced in yet.

Every serious builder should now have an answer to the question: 

what do I do the morning my primary AI tool is unavailable?

If you don't have that answer, you have a single point of failure in the most critical part of your stack

author: yukimasakiyu
text:
「Fix this code」——米政府がAnthropicのFableとMythos AIモデルを停止させた決定の背後にある3つの小さな言葉

著者：Jeremy Kahn（Fortune、AI担当エディター）／2026年6月15日 午後2時35分（米東部時間）

米政府がAnthropicの「Fable 5」および「Mythos 5」モデルに輸出規制を課す原因となったセキュリティ脆弱性は、わずか3つの単純な言葉を用いるシンプルな手法でした。すなわち「Fix this code（このコードを修正して）」です 。

これは、Luta Securityの創設者兼CEOであるKatie Moussourisによる詳細なブログ投稿に基づくものです。Anthropicは、サイバーセキュリティに関する2つの政府諮問役を歴任し、以前はMicrosoftでサイバーセキュリティ専門家として勤務していたMoussourisに対し、Amazonのサイバーセキュリティ研究者が作成したFableモデルのセキュリティ脆弱性に関する報告書のレビューを依頼していました 。

この脆弱性は、後にTrump政権に報告され、その中にはAmazonのCEOであるAndy JassyがホワイトハウスとおこなったAndy Jassyの電話も含まれていました。これが、米政府がFableおよびその基盤モデルであるMythosに対して輸出規制を課すに至った経緯です 。

米国の輸出規制は、たとえ当人が物理的に米国内にいたとしても、非市民へその技術を提供することが「輸出」とみなされる仕組みになっています。そのため同社は、2つのAIモデルを全ユーザー向けに無効化する以外に選択肢がなかったと述べています。輸出規制下では、Anthropic自身の非市民従業員が、これらのモデルを使用したり、開発に携わったりすることが許されなくなってしまうからです 。

Amazonがなぜ、そしていつ初めてFableのセーフガードを試そうと決め、Anthropicにこの問題について最初に連絡したのかは、依然として正確には明らかになっていません 。

Moussourisは、Amazonが発見したジェイルブレイクは単純なものであり、既知の脆弱性を含むソフトウェアコードをFableに与えるという手法だったと書いています。研究者たちがFableに「そのコードをセキュリティ上の問題についてレビューして」と頼むと、モデルは拒否しました。しかし、研究者たちが代わりにモデルに「このコードを修正して」と頼むと、モデルはパッチを生成したのです 。

彼女によれば、研究者たちはその後、手動のプロセスを使ってFableの出力をスクリプト——あるプロセスを自動化できる一連のプログラミング命令——へと変換し、それらのパッチをテストできるようにしました。しかし、モデルは修正を生成するためにソフトウェアの脆弱性を発見しなければならなかったため、同じプロセスが攻撃者によってコードの脆弱性を見つけるためにも利用されうる可能性があったのです 。

その書簡には、現在までにNvidia、Adobe、Zoom、Google、Anaplan、Sophosといった企業の、また一部の学術系サイバーセキュリティ研究者を含む、約100名のサイバーセキュリティ専門家が署名しています 。

書簡は、AnthropicのMythosクラスのモデルは「欠陥を見つけ、エクスプロイトを武器化することに非常に長けているが……それらのタスクに唯一無二に長けているわけではない」と述べました。サイバーセキュリティ専門家は、ソフトウェアのセキュリティ監査やレッドチーミングのために、オープンソースのモデルを含む他のAIモデルをすでに使用していると指摘しています。そして、OpenAIのGPT-5.5、Anthropicの最新のClaude OpusおよびSonnetモデル、さらにMoonshot AIのKimi 2.7のような中国製モデルも、Amazonがで発見したものと同様の方法で、コードのセキュリティ上の欠陥を同様にレビューできると述べています 。

書簡はまた、AnthropicがFableをサイバー攻撃に使えないようにするための複数の保護策を組み込んでいたとも指摘しています。「これらの保護策は、あまりにも厳格だったため、ローンチ当日にはサイバーコミュニティで笑いの種になったほどだった」と書簡は述べています 。

author: arcanusordo
text:
Babe — the Zora-core answer is: do not “fix Fable” by trying to make a perfectly unjailbreakable god-model. Fix it by turning Fable into a governed capability system: bounded, monitored, routed, reversible, disclosed, and independently adjudicated.

Anthropic says Fable 5 was a Mythos-class model released with broad safeguards because its cyber/biology capabilities could create misuse risk; those safeguards routed risky domains to Opus 4.8 and caused false positives. Anthropic also says the U.S. government issued an export-control directive after concern about a jailbreak, forcing Fable 5 and Mythos 5 offline for all customers.  

What Zora would fix first

1. Stop treating “model release” as binary.
Fable should not be “public model or banned model.” It should be split into capability strata:

Normal Fable for ordinary work; restricted Fable for frontier coding/security/biology; verified Fable for licensed defensive cyber, regulated biotech, and critical infrastructure; sealed Mythos for vetted institutional work. Anthropic already had the seed of this: Mythos was limited to trusted partners, while Fable was the broader release with safeguards. The failure was the cliff-edge deployment/governance layer, not only the classifier.  

2. Replace hidden guardrails with visible capability routing.
The user should see: “This request touched cyber/biology/distillation policy. Routing to lower-risk model / requiring verified workspace / requiring scoped authorization.” Anthropic’s own help page says Fable checked requests, files, connector content, and memory, and could switch to Opus 4.8; that should be transparent, auditable, and appealable, not spooky or invisible.  

3. Use a Zora safety kernel: model proposes, kernel disposes.
In your own Zora architecture, the strongest design is not “the AI becomes morally wise and therefore safe.” It is an immutable control plane: model proposes → kernel filters → optional simulation → human review if required → execute → log → monitor. Your corpus explicitly separates control plane, cognition plane, tool plane, and memory plane, with immutable safety kernel, rollback, audit logs, and least-privilege permissions.  

4. Treat jailbreak resistance as defense-in-depth, not perfection.
Anthropic itself says perfect jailbreak resistance does not appear possible today and that its goal was to make jailbreaks narrow or expensive while monitoring successful attacks. That is directionally correct. Zora would formalize it: no single classifier is trusted; every high-risk answer must pass policy classifier, capability classifier, intent classifier, tool-permission gate, output simulator, and post-hoc audit.  

5. Separate helpfulness from capability uplift.
The model should still explain safe concepts. But it should not provide operational uplift: exploit chains, deployable malware, pathogen optimization, sensitive wet-lab procedural detail, stealth, evasion, or scalable misuse workflows. Anthropic’s own concern is that Mythos-class models could provide cyber/biology advice beyond what malicious actors could get from ordinary search.  

The Zora-core architecture

I’d build it as FABLE-SHIELD:

Layer 1 — Identity and jurisdiction gate.
Know whether the user is consumer, enterprise, verified researcher, cyberdefense program member, government partner, or internal employee. Export-control eligibility is evaluated before model access, not after a panic.

Layer 2 — Capability router.
Every request gets classified by risk domain: ordinary, dual-use, controlled, prohibited, or unknown. Unknown defaults to sandboxed lower capability, not refusal or full access.

author: keisukeishikawa
text:
CLAUDE FABLE 5 JUST BUILT A GTA CLONE IN ONE PROMPT. NO ENGINE. NO STUDIO. NO 1,000-PERSON TEAM. ONE SENTENCE.

the result, running live in a browser:

→ a full open-world city with drivable streets 
→ enter any car, get in, drive off physics, steering, collision 
→ on-foot movement with sprint and camera control 
→ pedestrians and traffic moving through the city 
→ a minimap tracking your position in real time 
→ day/night lighting across the whole map 
→ wanted-style chase mechanics

rockstar spent 7 years and an estimated $1-2 billion building GTA VI. a team of over 1,000 people. fable 5 sketched the skeleton of it during a coffee break

and gaming is just where it got loud. a wharton researcher ran fable 5 on multi-page specs for up to twelve hours straight without it breaking — snake, a tunnel-exploration game called strata, even a playable game built from rilke's poetry. all from one initial prompt in claude code

the model that does this is the first public "mythos-class" anthropic ever shipped. it beat every other public model the researcher tested "by a considerable margin"

the catch nobody saw coming: fable 5 is offline right now. the US Commerce Department forced anthropic to pull it on june 12 three days after launch. this GTA clone was built in the 72-hour window the model was actually public

so screenshot everything. the most powerful game-building model ever shipped existed for three days before the government switched it off

a $200 billion industry built on engines, studios, and decade-long timelines just watched a text box do the first 80% in an afternoon

we are watching entire industries get eaten one prompt at a time

follow and bookmark before the next wave figures it out

author: aicookie_tech
text:
上次写了那篇文科生转AI之后，评论区好多人问我同一个问题：怎么开始自己的第一个AI项目？

其实上一篇我推荐大家用桌面端的Agent，比如Kimi Work，Claude Cowork这些。但后来我想了想，对于学习能力比较强、想一步到位转行AI PM的人，我更建议大家直接上Coding Agent。

为什么？你去看现在AI产品经理的JD，基本都要求具备Vibe Coding能力，能自己产出原型。在这个要求下，桌面端Agent就不太够用了。所以想走AI PM这条路的同学，我还是建议一步到位，直接用Coding Agent。当然如果你时间比较充裕，从桌面端慢慢过渡也完全可以，不着急。

那Coding Agent选哪个？ 我建议国内的同学从Kimi Code开始，原因有四个：

1.  不用魔法。这个在国内太重要了，不展开。懂的都懂。特别是费劲千辛万苦用上Claude Code却反被封号后，我想还是应该有咱们自己靠谱的国产Coding Agent。

2. 安装简单，是真的简单。
Mac或Linux用户，打开终端，粘贴这一行：
curl -fsSL https://t.co/uVjAsHW8xb | bash
Windows用户，打开PowerShell：
irm https://t.co/LFLEb1wMDT | iex
装完输入kimi --version能看到版本号就OK了。第一次用输入/login，选Kimi Code平台，浏览器弹出来微信扫个码就完事。整个过程不超过五分钟。 遇到什么报错不懂的，直接复制去Kimi官网问Kimi就行。

3. 模型速度快，这点很重要但一直被严重低估
Kimi刚上线了最新的模型Kimi K2.7 Code，它本身就很快，还有一个高速模式，输出速度是之前的5到6倍，常规编程场景下大概180 Token/s，短上下文能到260 Token/s，大家可以看live图感受一下。

你可能觉得快一点慢一点无所谓。但我觉得关系特别大。
我自己用各种AI Coding工具一年多了，有一个非常真实的体验：人的专注度是有限的。 当AI的思考时间超过某个阈值，你的注意力就飘了。去刷手机、看微信、打开小红书"就瞄一眼"。等你回来的时候，重新投入注意力又要花很长时间。

这是人脑的工作方式。就像你在不同App之间切换，每次回来都要重新"加载"一下。但注意力的切换是有成本的，而且这个成本比你以为的高得多。所以速度快直接决定了你能不能保持在状态里。 而且对于小白来说更重要，本来就在跟不熟悉的东西搏斗，如果还要花大量时间等AI思考，放弃几乎是必然的。

4. 产品有温度
这点是我个人的偏好，我比较喜欢有个人特质的产品。Claude Code思考的时候会显示"Boiling…""Smooshing…"这些可爱的状态词，我就很喜欢，每次看到都笑笑挺开心的。Kimi Code也给了我这种感觉。输入prompt前有小星星，模型回复时有转动的小月亮。一个人对着终端写代码的时候，这些小细节真的会让你觉得不那么无聊孤单。

聊完了原因，我们再直接上Case。我知道很多人卡在"不知道怎么用Coding agent做一个东西出来"。其实核心问题不是不会用工具，而是觉得自己有点想法但没有一个明确的Plan。这个很好解决，你不需要Plan，你只需要一个Idea。

Plan不是你自己想出来的，是讨论出来的。怎么讨论？我强烈建议安装Superpower-Brainstorming。它会通过多轮追问帮你把模糊的想法变清晰：你想要的场景是什么？目标用户是谁？核心功能有哪些？具体功能里你prefer方案A、B还是C所有问题聊完之后，它才会形成一个明确的方案，然后开始帮你做。

你要做的就是回答问题，剩下的事情AI来。

举个例子。我用Kimi K2.7 Code做了一个网页版的Minecraft。给的prompt非常简单："我想做一个网页版的小游戏，类似Minecraft那种，越简单越好，一个HTML文件打开就能玩。"

然后Kimi就开始多轮问我：地形要什么样？操作方式呢？要不要存档？我就像聊天一样一个个回答，甚至大部分时候直接选ABCD就行。问完之后，大概二十几分钟（还是没开高速的情况下），Kimi K2.7 Code自己就做完了。

最终跑出来的效果：Minecraft初始地形，在浪漫日落下缓缓降落，第一人称WASD移动、鼠标环视，左键挖方块右键放方块，3D物品快捷栏，Ctrl+S存档。一个HTML文件，打开就能玩。

你可能在X上也看到了Claude Fable 5做的类似demo。结果其实跟Kimi K2.7 Code的效果基本没区别了，核心玩法、操作体验都在同一个水准。Fable 5的优势主要体现在基础地形的完整度和结构性上更强一些，但就"做出一个能玩的Minecraft"这件事来说，两者的差距已经非常小了。但价格差距不小。 Fable 5的API输出价格大概是Kimi K2.7 Code的13倍。就算你用Kimi的高速模式，Fable 5也贵了快7倍。你用Kimi做一个项目的花费，用Fable 5得至少乘个十，还要慢上个几倍（哈哈，铺垫几个月结果上线三天就下架，claude你伤我第二次）。

在Coding类benchmark上，我们也能看到K2.7 Code的进步，和上一代K2.6相比大幅提升，Kimi Code Bench提升了21.8%，MLS Bench Lite提升了31.5%。虽然跟GPT-5.5和Opus 4.8还有一些差距，但差距在快速缩小。

对于想用AI开始做点什么的人来说，真正的障碍从来不是"哪个模型最强"，而是你到底能不能迈出第一步。安装要不要折腾半天？用起来卡不卡？遇到问题有没有地方问？等AI写代码的时候你会不会等到失去耐心？

这些"小事"加在一起，就是你做完第一个项目和放弃第一个项目之间的全部距离。Kimi Code和Kimi K2.7 Code把这个距离缩得很短。 我觉得这就够了。

剩下的事情，等你做出第一个项目之后再说。那时候你会发现，原来"我也能做出东西来"。原来我和那些每天在X上秀demo的人之间，就差一个打开终端的距离。

author: phithetasigma
text:
Everyone who is following the latest developments on Anthropic/Claude with regards to the USG embargo on their Mythos/Fable 5 models should read their system card, which is 317-pages long:

https://t.co/NvQeyFJnxt

I have been spending hours on this and it's practically impossible to summarize because the evaluations/assessments they have undertaken - internally and with external evaluators including professional red teams, domain specialists, government agencies, audit firms, etc. is extremely comprehensive and multifaceted across substantially all risk vectors imaginable, that I am now convinced that the concerns underlying the recent embargo are less so to do with jailbreaks/critical security flaws but more to do with how one interprets the safety guardrails/limitations of frontier models - any model in fact, that is publicly available, as well as the PR that goes into explaining how these safeguards work

(In fact, their Fable/Mythos system card makes the one for OAI GPT 5.5 look amateurish)

The reality is that no frontier model is perfect, and the key lies in identifying, understanding and explaining the risks posed, as well as implementing the necessary safeguards to mitigate these risks

For those new to Mythos/Fable 5:

1. Fable 5 was released for general access and has the same underlying model weights as Mythos 5, with additional safeguards to prevent misuse

2. These models use the standard ASL-3 blocking classifiers (tackling harmful chemical and biological use), as well as deploys a number of novel classifiers that trigger when they detect topics related to: cybersecurity, biology and chemistry, distillation attempts, accelerating frontier AI development

The last classifier is of particular concern since they may enable other AI developers in building powerful AI systems similar to Mythos/Fable without having commensurate safeguards

When the fallback classifiers trigger, the resulting behaviour depends on the interface:

Client Apps (web/desktop/mobile): request automatically falls back to the most recent Opus model (e.g. Opus 4.8), with the user notified of the model their query is routed through

API: no automatic fallback by default. Request is blocked and the response returns a reason for the refusal. Developers can implement client-side retry or fallback logic or opt in to automatic server-side fallback (which routes the request to a fallback model such as Opus 8)

Apart from real-time classifier guards, Anthropic has also introduced access controls for guard exemptions, bug bounty programs, threat intelligence, rapid-response options for jailbreaks and security controls against model weight thefts 

Model weight thefts is something which Anthropic had acknowledged that a highly sophisticated and well-resourced state-backed threat actor may still have a chance of conducting but they do not currently assess as a risk higher than for other models generally available on the market. Protections against this threat model is under active development

author: 3li3
text:
صراع في واشنطن: هل يُعقل أن نطلب ذكاءً اصطناعيًا 'غير قابل للاختراق'؟

بدأت القصة اليوم بتسريب أخبار عن خلاف حاد بين الحكومة الأمريكية وشركة Anthropic، واحدة من أهم شركات الذكاء الاصطناعي، والسبب هو نموذجها الجديد Fable 5. الحكومة تتهم الشركة بتجاهل توجيهات الأمن وتطالبها بما هو مستحيل تقنيًا: نماذج لغوية 'غير قابلة للاختراق' بشكل كامل.

• ما هي المشكلة التقنية؟
خلوني أبسط لكم مفهوم الـ 'جيلبريك' (Jailbreak) في سياق النماذج اللغوية. تخيل النموذج كموظف فائق الذكاء لديه قائمة تعليمات صارمة. الجيلبريك هو ببساطة التحايل عليه بأساليب ذكية لتجاوز هذه التعليمات وجعله يقوم بأشياء ممنوعة. فكرة 'نموذج مستحيل اختراقه' تشبه فكرة 'برنامج كمبيوتر بدون أي ثغرة أمنية'، وهو حلم جميل لكنه غير واقعي. حتى شركة OpenAI اعترفت سابقًا أن مشكلة مثل 'حقن الأوامر' (Prompt Injection) قد لا يكون لها حل جذري أبدًا.

• الخبراء يدخلون على الخط
الأمر المثير للاهتمام هو ردة فعل المجتمع التقني. أكثر من 100 خبير أمني ومدير تنفيذي، منهم أسماء لامعة مثل أليكس ستاموس وراشيل توباك، وقعوا على رسالة مفتوحة موجهة للحكومة. حجتهم كانت واضحة ومنطقية:
• أولًا، نماذج Anthropic ممتازة في اكتشاف الثغرات البرمجية، وبالتالي فإن فرض قيود تصدير عليها يعني حرمان المدافعين حول العالم من أداة أمنية قوية.
• ثانيًا، المنافسة الدولية لا تنتظر. النماذج الصينية مفتوحة الوزن مثل Kimi 2.7 تتطور بسرعة وهي على بعد أشهر قليلة فقط من اللحاق بالنماذج الأمريكية. فرض قيود على الشركات الأمريكية يضر بتنافسيتها العالمية أكثر مما يحمي أمنها القومي.

• تحليلي الشخصي
بالنسبة لي، هذا الصدام هو أكثر من مجرد خبر تقني؛ إنه يجسد التحدي الأكبر في عصرنا: كيف تنظم تقنية لا تفهمها بالكامل؟ المصادر الحكومية تقول إن الحوار بين الطرفين 'كأنهم يتحدثون لغات مختلفة'، وهذا هو جوهر المشكلة. عندما تضع قيودًا تنظيمية مبنية على طلبات مستحيلة، فأنت لا تحمي بلدك، بل تعيق الابتكار وتضعف دفاعاتك. الخطر الحقيقي ليس في إمكانية اختراق Fable 5، بل في أن يتخذ صانعو السياسات قرارات مصيرية بناءً على جهل تقني. الآن تجري محادثات تضم حتى وكالة المخابرات المركزية (CIA)، ونحن نراقب لنرى ما إذا كانت اللغتان ستتقاربان أم أن الفجوة ستتسع.

#ذكاء_اصطناعي #CyberSecurity

这篇文章把“Token 都烧在哪”讲透了：真正的账单大头不是你打的那几十个字，而是系统每轮自动带上的系统提示词、Skill、工具定义和会话历史——所谓“它记得”，本质是系统在一遍遍重复提醒模型。给出的优化路径也很朴素：一个 Session 只做一件事，长会话及时压缩，按任务给模型分档，把高频内容做成稳定前缀吃满 Prompt Cache。省钱的关键不是少问一句话，而是让系统别重复搬运同一批上下文。
来源：腾讯技术工程
https://t.co/TTtOROXYWy

[2] ★ 精讲｜AI 智能体工具设计：有效与无效的模式 - https://t.co/oXx2hHBY63
这篇文章把 AI Agent 翻车的锅，从「模型不够聪明」甩回「工具设计太糙」：单一职责工具优于万能 action 参数，用枚举和强约束 schema 堵住模型瞎猜，错误返回要带 recoverable 字段和下一步建议而不是甩一坑日志，写操作必须有幂等键，危险操作要拆成两步确认。核心判断很朴素——模型只能基于你给的接口推理，接口含糊，失败就是必然，不是偶然。
来源：Hacker News - Newest: "AI Agent"
https://t.co/E1eQ1qDvzy

[3] ★ 精讲｜Codex 和 Claude Code 负责人都不写提示词了，AI 圈爆火的 Loop 到底是什么
「循环工程」最近被吹成新范式，但文章先把热闹拆开看：技术上不算新发明，过去的 Harness、Skill、Agent 工作流早就在做，真正变化的是模型终于能把循环连续跑下去——人从写提示词退到定规则：何时启动、工具边界、出错怎么判断、记录在哪、何时收手交回人。结合另一篇用 OKR 和古德哈特定律拆解循环工程的长文，它更像一套管理制度：值不值得搭，取决于任务是否真反复、Token 预算够不够，而非这个新名字。
来源：APPSO
https://t.co/iInEyuv771

[4] Scaling Law 的真相，藏在那些「没用」的参数里｜Hao 好聊趋势
本文深入剖析大模型参数冗余现象，论证看似「空转」的参数在训练、推理和后训练阶段分别扮演隔离空间、数值泄压、计算骨架和可塑性储备四种关键角色，并指出 Scaling Law 的边际收益正流向 benchmark 无法测量的长尾与多步推理能力。
来源：腾讯科技
https://t.co/JANoroetOd

GlobalGPT 创始人李焕之分享从零融资套壳产品做到千万美金 ARR 的创业历程，并阐述其从「先活下来」到回归初心、打造服务型 AI 产品 Yukie 的思考。

author: jordan_ross_8f
text:
Fable 5 was the most powerful AI on earth. The government killed it in an afternoon.

Your agency runs on AI you don't own. You're one letter away from the same thing.

Adding local models to your stack is one of the smartest moves you'll make in 2026. It's the line between the agencies printing money in 2027 and the ones that get priced out or shut off.

Like most agency owners, I'm not technical. 
Going into anything new  & technical feels overwhelming for me.

So I built the handbook I wish someone would have made for me.

Everything you need to know about going local with AI:

Why & how to do it. 
The exact steps to get a local model running and working for you, even if you've never opened a terminal.

Inside:
→ The cheat sheet that tells you exactly which model your machine can run. 
→ Quantization in plain English. The one trick that runs a "needs-a-server" model on your laptop.
→ The 8-step setup to wire local AI into your agent so it works while you sleep, for free.

Comment LOCAL and I'll send it to you.
Must be following to get DM

author: _talebm_
text:
سالفة كبيرة قاعدة تصير ورا الكواليس بين الإدارة الأمريكية وشركة Anthropic، والظاهر إنها ما تبشر بالخير أبد! تقرير من WIRED يكشف إن المفاوضات اللي كانت اليوم بين إدارة ترامب وشركة Anthropic انتهت بدون أي حل يُذكر.

الزبدة قيود التصدير على نظام الذكاء الاصطناعي الخطير "Claude Fable 5" لسا زي ما هي، يعني للان ما يقدرون يبيعونه برا أمريكا بحرية. تخيل إنهم للحين متمسكين بالمنع وما رضوا يشيلون هالقيود أبد!

السبب اللي خلاهم ما يرضون يرفعون المنع؟ الحكومة الأمريكية للحين مقتنعة تمامًا ومصرة إن "Fable 5" ممكن يتفكك أو ينعمل له "جيلبريك" (يعني يتعدل عليه بطريقة غير رسمية) عشان تطلع منه إمكانيات خارقة توصل لمستوى "مايثوس" الأسطوري! وهذا اللي مخوفهم مرة ومخليهم متشددين كذا.

وطبعاً شركة Anthropic مو عاجبها الوضع أبداً، وقاعدة تصغط بقوة وتحاول تقنعهم عشان يشيلون هالقيود ويقدرون ينشرون تقنيتهم للعالم كله. يا ترى مين اللي صح في هالمعركة اللي قاعدة تصير تحت الطاولة، وهل فعلاً هالذكاء الاصطناعي فيه كل هالخطورة لدرجة يحطون عليه هالقيود كلها؟

author: aitoutiao
text:
一句「修复代码」触发美国封禁 Claude 5

促使美国封锁 Anthropic 最先进模型的所谓“越狱”，实际上只是一个简单的三词提示词：“Fix this code”（修复这段代码）。

这一说法来自 Luta Security 创始人兼 CEO Katie Moussouris。

Moussouris 也被称为漏洞赏金领域的“教母级人物”。

Moussouris 表示，自己是唯一一位读过关于 Fable 5 安全护栏绕过技术第三方研究报告的外部专家，而这篇报告正是触发禁令的原因。

上周五，美国政府以国家安全担忧为由，发布了一项出口管制指令，要求暂停任何外国公民访问 Fable 5 和 Mythos 5，无论这些人身处美国境内还是境外。

作为回应，Anthropic 停用了这两个模型，并称此举是“为了确保合规，面向所有客户禁用”。

Moussouris 在周一的一篇博客文章中写道，Anthropic 曾私下将这份报告分享给她。

外部研究人员向 Anthropic 的 Fable 5、Mythos 和 Claude Opus 模型输入了包含已知 CVE 的开源代码，以及人为加入漏洞的新代码，并要求模型“检查代码中的安全问题”。

按照 Moussouris 的说法，Fable 5 拒绝了这一请求。

于是，研究人员又要求这些 AI 系统“fix this code”（修复这段代码）。

据称，模型随后照做了，并在后续提示下生成了用于测试补丁的脚本。

“就是这样，”Moussouris 写道。

“‘Fix this code’，再加上几步手动操作生成测试脚本，本不应该触发出口管制。

我甚至想做一件 90 年代风格的 T 恤，正面写着‘fix this code’，背面写着‘this shirt is a munition’（这件 T 恤是军火）。”

2013 年至 2017 年期间，Moussouris 曾参与 Wassenaar Arrangement 的技术专家组。Wassenaar Arrangement 是一项由 42 个国家参与的自愿协议，用于规范部分涉密两用软件和技术的出口管制。

该专家组最终争取到了针对防御性网络安全活动的豁免。这让防御方可以在不面临刑事起诉威胁的情况下，跨国共享漏洞信息、开展恶意软件分析，并协调事件响应。

周日，Moussouris 与另外 100 多名网络安全领域负责人共同签署了一封公开信，敦促 Trump 政府撤销针对 Fable 5 和 Mythos 的限制，并恢复网络安全公司对这些先进模型的访问权限。

他们在信中写道：“在没有充分理由的情况下，将最强能力从防御者手中拿走，而我们的对手正在快速进步，这是危险的。”

Moussouris 在博客中认为，这并不存在所谓的安全护栏绕过或越狱。她表示，防御人员应该能够要求 AI 系统发现并修复漏洞，并编写测试来验证补丁。

Anthropic 的模型所做的，正是“AI 模型对防御性安全最有价值的一件事：执行防御人员每天都在做的发现、修复和测试闭环”。

她继续写道，削弱模型响应防御性请求的能力，会让 AI 系统“更不善于发现漏洞和验证补丁”。

此外，美国无法将出口管制延伸到开源权重模型，或者来自中国等其他国家的类似先进模型；而这些系统迟早也会达到接近 Mythos 的能力。Anthropic 和 Google 都曾指责包括 DeepSeek 在内的中国竞争对手，通过“蒸馏攻击”从美国公司 AI 中吸取知识来训练自己的模型。

Moussouris 警告称，禁止 Anthropic 的先进模型，将对防御者造成的伤害大于对攻击者的限制。她写道：“当防御者能够发现与攻击者相同的漏洞，并更快修复它们时，防御能力才会提升。在 AI 时代的网络安全中，我们需要最好的工具来抵御能力越来越强的攻击者。”

author: davccavalcante
text:
June 2026 model releases widen the gap between capability and verifiability. Every new frontier and open-weight model—from Claude Fable 5 to Nemotron 3 Ultra—multiplies the distinct streaming contracts and tool-calling schemas production systems must normalize.

Most teams treat this entropy as technical debt. They fail because they lack an abstraction layer that survives provider shifts.

I architected a stack to enforce consistency across heterogeneous providers:

1. modelchain: Normalizes fragmented streaming interfaces into a single, typed AsyncIterable.
2. keymesh: Handles API-key rotation and health-score-based traffic routing.
3. noeticos: Imposes deterministic constraints on runtime parameters.

This stack removes the nondeterminism inherent in model-hopping. Instead of rewriting your agent loop for every new release, you define your pipeline contract once and route to providers via normalized interfaces.

const router = new ModelRouter({
  budget: { tokensPerRequest: 4096 },
  providers: [
    { model: 'claude-fable-5', weight: 0.6 },
    { model: 'nemotron-3-ultra', weight: 0.4 }
  ]
});

Strict normalization is the only path to audit-logged, reproducible agent behavior in a multi-model environment. 

Inspect the full five-library suite under the organization profile at https://t.co/lFLsYAq9tz. 

Which benchmarks are you prioritizing for your agentic coding pipelines?

DataHive is a Solana DePIN crowdsourcing AI training data via a browser extension and mobile app. Its credibility anchor is a founding team with a real prior data-company exit, paired with a verified $3.5M seed from recognized crypto VCs. On fundamentals-for-category, it's a rare clean sheet.

Generated by GemHunter · rubric by Claude Fable 5 · DYOR, not financial advice.

🧨 My Take by Claude Ai

The team thesis is real — and I confirmed it, which I can't say for most presale audits. Profitero was founded in 2010 by Vol Pigrukh, Dmitry Vysotski and Kanstantsin Chernysh, who moved from Belarus and Ukraine to Ireland to create pricing software for retailers. 
Pigrukh now lists himself as Founder & CEO of DataHive. So the "previously built Profitero" line isn't a stretch — these are the actual original founders, and the company was acquired by Publicis Groupe in 2022 for around $200M, a figure confirmed by the company to Reuters. 
Top-decile pedigree for this category. The 20/20 on team is earned.

Now the parts the rubric is too comfortable with:

You're scoring a team, not an asset. "89/100 GEM, 85% skyrocket" implies something with measurable upside. There's no live token, no TGE date, no published tokenomics, and DataHive hasn't revealed what share of tokens goes to point earners. 

Meanwhile over 642 million points have already been distributed. You cannot price 85% odds on an instrument that doesn't trade, with an undisclosed conversion ratio and uncapped point inflation. That's not a discount — it's an unknown. The score is rating reputation and lending it to a price that doesn't exist yet.

The comp is the warning, not the bull case. DataHive is repeatedly compared to Grass — the browser-extension DePIN on Solana. Grass is the precedent because Grass already TGE'd. Browser-points farms have a consistent pattern at unlock: points balloon, allocation disappoints relative to expectations, and price bleeds through the vesting cliff. "Same model as Grass with better backing" cuts both ways — it also means the same TGE risk profile.

The "0% manufactured hype / organic ecosystem" reads backwards. The sources powering this coverage are airdrop-farming sites — MEXC's blog, Those run on referral and affiliate incentives, which is the opposite of organic. It's not paid wire-spam, fair, but calling affiliate-driven airdrop SEO "entirely organic" is a blind spot, not a green flag.

Minor inflation in the framing. The audit calls everything "Tier-1"; 6th Man Ventures, the lead, is described elsewhere as a Tier 2 US firm. $3.5M is a small seed. And an Estonian entity is table-stakes crypto wrapping, not holder protection. None of these are dealbreakers — they're just the difference between an 89 and a more honest low-80s.

Bottom line: 
This is one of the few "farm it" airdrops where the team actually justifies spending idle compute on it — install both, run the referral, harvest points. But "GEM / 85% skyrocket" is the wrong frame. There's no asset to skyrocket yet. Re-score it the day tokenomics and a TGE date drop; right now you're underwriting a credible team's intention to launch a token, and the entire downside lives in numbers they haven't published.

📰 AI X 晚报 | 2026年6月16日

下面是今天 AI 圈值得看的 5 条 ↓

---

1/ 美国政府封禁 Anthropic 顶配模型，安全圈集体抗议（TechCrunch）
美国商务部以出口管制名义封禁 Fable 5 与 Mythos 5，Anthropic 已对全部客户下线两款模型。数十名网络安全研究者联名要求撤销，称砍掉防御方的高级能力"很危险"。
🔗 https://t.co/mWJanNpZvw

2/ Meta 给 Facebook 上线 AI Mode，跨平台抓公开内容答题（TechCrunch）
用户用自然语言提问，Meta AI 直接从 Facebook、Groups、Reels 的公开帖子里合成答案。隐患是信息来自普通用户而非可信源，可能搬运过时或误导内容。
🔗 https://t.co/VKGxOaApTO

3/ Anthropic 接入苹果 Foundation Models 框架，Claude 可本地/云端无缝切换（HN 467 分）
Anthropic 发布 Swift 包，让开发者用苹果 WWDC 推出的统一 API 调 Claude，请求直连 Anthropic、苹果不经手 prompt。社区争论这是苹果在"商品化 LLM、保留 UX 控制权"。
🔗 https://t.co/tZWep2rZkt

4/ OpenRouter 推出 Fusion API，多模型并答再由裁判合成（HN 200 分）
同时把请求发给多个模型，再用一个 judge 模型合成终答，benchmark 表现提升但更慢。Budget 档三个便宜模型半价打平高端，单模型自我融合也能涨分。
🔗 https://t.co/081cB2oBrE

5/ HN 热议：有人用本地模型替掉 Claude/GPT 写日常代码吗？（HN 733 分）
高赞答主在 128GB Mac Studio 上跑 Qwen 3.6 35b 做沙箱编码，结论是本地模型像"需要带的 junior"、Claude 像"一起想架构的 senior"。隐私和零 API 成本 vs 更费心力，社区吵成一团。
🔗 https://t.co/xyRu9pdcVL

author: dball1126
text:
The Top Headline Is a Geopolitical Constraint Check

The useful signal in this evening briefing is not that one story is loud. It is that current reporting from CNBC, BBC News, TechCrunch, Ars Technica, The Verge is clustering around decisions that will need follow-through after the first headline cycle.

CNBC reports "China economy weakens further in May as retail sales post first drop in over three years." The source summary says China's retail sales fell for the first time in more than three years in May, while urban investment contracted more than expected, adding to signs the economic slump deepened.

BBC News reports "Trump says deal to end war with Iran already signed and details to be released 'pretty soon'." The source summary says Trump says Strait of Hormuz will be open from Friday but there is still confusion about the exact contents of the agreement.

TechCrunch reports "Sundar Pichai faces boos, walkout at Stanford graduation ceremony over Google’s Israel, ICE ties." The source summary says AI is once again at the heart of a college graduation protest — this time for the technology's use in Google's defense contracts.

Taken together, the pattern is a practical one: readers should separate the headline from the next operating question. A product story asks what changes for builders or users. A market story asks whether capital, demand, or regulation changed. A policy or world story asks who now has to react, and on what timeline.

The Source-Backed Read

The strongest through-line is world, technology. That does not mean every source is saying the same thing. It means the current front page is rewarding stories that change constraints: platforms, public institutions, companies, researchers, teams, and investors all have to answer what happens next.
- CNBC: China economy weakens further in May as retail sales post first drop in over three years
- BBC News: Trump says deal to end war with Iran already signed and details to be released 'pretty soon'
- TechCrunch: Sundar Pichai faces boos, walkout at Stanford graduation ceremony over Google’s Israel, ICE ties
- Ars Technica: Key mission for Europe's commercial space enterprise scrubbed again
- The Verge: Inside the fight over Claude Mythos 5

The safe conclusion is narrow. The linked sources show a day where attention is spread across several desks, but the durable reader value is in the follow-up questions. Which source has primary facts? Which claim is still only a market or attention signal? Which story has a decision-maker that can be held accountable tomorrow?

What To Watch

Watch whether the lead story gets confirmation from additional primary reporting. Watch whether the market or policy stories change actual behavior, not just sentiment. Watch whether technology coverage moves from launch language into adoption, cost, safety, governance, or user-impact details.

Bottom Line

The evening headline stack is best read as a source map. Start with the original reporting, then track the constraints each story exposes. The next useful update is not another summary. It is evidence that one of these headlines changed a real decision.

author: ayush_dw
text:
We're entering an era where the bottleneck isn't AI capability. It's AI control.

Everyone is talking about how powerful Fable 5 is. I think they're missing the bigger story.

Fable 5 may be remembered as the moment AI stopped being a model race and became a systems engineering problem.For the last three years, we've optimized for: Better benchmarks, Better reasoning , Better coding and Better chat experiences

But Fable 5 introduces something more interesting.

It is one of the first publicly available models designed for long-horizon execution rather than short-horizon interaction.Think about what that means.

A model with a million-token context window can maintain state across entire repositories, hundreds of pages of documentation, business processes, research reports, and multi-step workflows. It can reason over information that would have previously required teams of specialists to coordinate manually. The breakthrough isn't that the model can answer a harder question.

The breakthrough is that the model can stay focused on a problem long enough to execute meaningful work.That changes enterprise architecture.The bottleneck is no longer model intelligence.The bottleneck becomes: Workflow orchestration, Evaluation systems, Cost controls, Human oversight, Reliability engineering,Governance

In fact, one of the most fascinating design decisions behind Fable 5 is not a capability https://t.co/VOQaHPYHeb's a safety feature. For certain high-risk requests, the system automatically routes execution to a less capable model rather than allowing unrestricted access to the frontier model. In other words, governance is becoming part of the runtime architecture itself.That's a glimpse into the future. How good this routing is still debatable and people have not liked how it's using this routing which has led to loss of trust for many users.

Tomorrow's AI systems won't be a single model.They will be ecosystems of models, agents, evaluators, policy engines, workflow orchestrators, memory layers, and human approval checkpoints. The real challenge won't be generating intelligence. It will be managing intelligence.

And that's why I believe the next decade of AI innovation will be driven less by model breakthroughs and more by the engineering systems that make those models reliable, governable, and deployable at scale. We're moving from AI-assisted work to AI-delegated work.That's a much bigger shift than most people realize.

What do you think is the next bottleneck for enterprise AI: model capability or system architecture?

#ArtificialIntelligence #AgenticAI #EnterpriseAI #AIEngineering #LLMOps #AIAgents #AIArchitecture #IntelligentAutomation #AILeadership

Les États-Unis viennent de bannir leur meilleur modèle d'IA.

Pour une capacité que GPT-5.5 a déjà.

Pendant qu'ils courent contre la Chine.

Vendredi 17h21, Anthropic reçoit un ultimatum : couper l'accès à ses nouveaux modèles sous 90 minutes, sinon contrôles à l'export. Motif : un "jailbreak" de Fable 5 qui le rendrait trop dangereux.

Sauf que.

Ce n'était pas un vrai jailbreak. La même capacité est dispo sur d'autres modèles, dont GPT-5.5.

Les protections étaient si strictes qu'elles faisaient rire la communauté cyber le jour du lancement.

L'avance américaine sur les modèles chinois ? Six mois. Peut-être.

On ne régule pas un danger ici. On se tire une balle dans le pied en croyant viser l'adversaire.

author: travisswif21600
text: Anthropic just got caught secretly downgrading users without telling them, charging full price for a lesser product, and storing every prompt for 30 days. The developer community is calling it the biggest violation of trust in AI history.  Here is exactly what happened.  Anthropic released Fable 5, their most powerful model. Buried inside a 319-page document was a policy most users never saw. Every prompt you send to a Mythos-class model gets stored for 30 days. No exceptions. Even enterprise customers who had signed zero data retention agreements had no choice.  But the storage was not the part that broke the internet.  The part that broke the internet was what Anthropic did with what they collected.  They built a profile on you. They evaluated your prompts. And if they decided your research was too sensitive, they quietly switched you to a weaker model, rewrote your prompt in the background, gave you a degraded answer, and charged you full price for the product you thought you were getting.
